_comment: Hand-verified spec fixtures for the typed spec system (plan Phase 5).
Each case names a real product id in data/catalog.json and the values the
pipeline MUST produce. check_golden.py asserts them after a normalize run.
expect            — asserted always (title/vendor-sourced, deterministic).
expect_reference  — asserted only when the optional pcpartdb reference
index exists (data/pcpartdb/index.json is a rebuilt,
git-ignored cache; without it Tier 0 is off by design).
expect_null       — fields that must be UNKNOWN (null/absent). This is how
a wrong value is pinned as a regression: e.g. an air
cooler must never claim water_cooled/radiator_size_mm.
Values are in the schema's canonical unit (units live in the field name).
Anchors (Oct 2026): a case may carry `anchors` - the vendor listing keys,
part numbers and model it was hand-verified against. Product ids are rebuilt
from whichever listings exist that day, so a vendor delist/merge/split moves
them. The gate resolves a case by its own product_id first and ONLY by it (a
live product whose values changed is a regression, not churn), and falls back
to anchors only when that id is gone. Repair after a normalize run with:
python -m scraper.specs.golden.check_golden --update-anchors --apply
Anchors are append-only evidence - a stale key is never deleted, only joined.
`expect.part_numbers` is CONTAINMENT, not equality: a product may gain a
manufacturer model code (specs/build.py with_model_code) and that is not a
regression.
2026-09-29 Plonter drop removed 3 cases whose products left the catalog
(mpn:cooler_air:a40pro, sku:cooler_air:peerlessassassin120digitalargbwhite,
mpn:psu:cp9020251eu — all Plonter-only singletons). No surviving product
carries the same rich specs (0 cooler_air products with sockets+fan left),
so the socket-list and printed-part-number rules are unpinned until vendor
data exercises them again. The rules themselves are untouched.
2026-10-29: the MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi case (its only source was
1pc:179926, an EAN-keyed one-vendor product) was replaced by the four-vendor
Gigabyte B850 Aorus Elite WIFI7 - see that case's `_pins`. That is exactly
the churn the anchors exist to absorb.

cases.name: Samsung 2TB 990 PRO NVMe M.2 SSD
cases._pins: Printed MPN spelling. Samsung/Plonter print 'MZ-V9P2T0BW'; the product id stays the compact key (mzv9p2t0bw). This case used to be reproducible only while a 1PC listing that carried a printed MPN existed — Plonter's 403 day (Sep 2026) dropped it and the piped value flipped to 'MZV9P2T0BW', which is exactly the flake this pins down.

cases.name: Gigabyte B850 Aorus Elite WIFI7
cases._pins: 2026-10-29: replaces the MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi case, whose only source (1pc:179926) delisted. That listing also carried the EAN-as-part-number assertion, which is not pinned here any more: the board is sold by four vendors, so one vendor's churn cannot retire the case. `expect.part_numbers` is containment, so the model code joining the list is not a regression.

cases.name: Verbatim VI550 S3 2TB 2.5" SSD
cases._pins: TB -> GB scaling: the vendor cell reads '2TB', so a naive number parse shipped 2GB (and the <16GB guard then dropped it).

cases.name: ASUS GeForce RTX 5070 12GB OC
cases._pins: GPU chipset canonical form. The board rule for chipset used to reject every multi-word GPU chip, which was 87% of the catalogue. Re-pinned 2026-10-21 to a 3-vendor product (1PC/Ivory/TMS): the previous pins, MSI mpn:gpu:4711377303927 and then mpn:gpu:4711377308175, left the catalogue when their only listings (1PC sold out, then ivory:135057 / 1pc:203118 delisted) disappeared.

models: Dual GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GDDR7 OC Edition

cases.name: AMD Threadripper 7960X Tray
cases._pins: Socket canonicalization: vendors print 'AMD STR5 (LGA4844)', which used to be dropped (or, worse, read as the package name in the parentheses).

cases.name: Thermalright Peerless Assassin Vision MAX White ARGB
cases._pins: Oct 2026 coverage pass: Ivory prints 'מידות כ-: גובה 164 רוחב 110 עומק 125' (consistent across scrapes since Sep 2026), which the new DIMS_CELL mapping reads as height_mm 164. The previous 170 came from no surviving source (title has no height, Tier-0 has no entry) and was stale. 2026-10-24: Ivory dropped the Black listing (81425602213-2), so the pin moved to the White sibling (same page layout, same cooler).

models: Peerless Assassin 120 Vision MAX ARGB WHITE

cases.name: Corsair Frame 4000D White
cases._pins: Phase 1d: Tier 0.5 manufacturer page (corsair.com) states the clearances; a retailer value must never outrank it.

cases.name: Corsair iCUE 5000D Airflow RGB Black
cases._pins: Phase 1d: second manufacturer-sourced case (5000D clears 420mm GPUs / 170mm coolers per corsair.com).

cases.name: ASUS Prime B550-Plus
cases._pins: Phase 1c/1d: no Wi-Fi/Bluetooth board is recorded as "No" (never null, never "None" - a coerce placeholder).
